entityDescription: The Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (NCU) was founded in 1945. It is one of the largest universities in Poland, currently comprising 17 faculties (including 3 medical faculties at Collegium Medicum UMK in Bydgoszcz). It provides graduate and postgraduate courses for almost 30 000 students, offering education in over 80 fields of study, 100 specialisations and 50 postgraduate courses. The university employs 4300 staff on both Toruń and Bydgoszcz campuses, over half of whom are academic teachers. NCU alumni now number nearly 200 000. The university participates in student and staff exchange programs at both international (the Erasmus program) and national (the MOST program) levels. It develops studies in cooperation with universities abroad and is currently collaborating with the universities in Angers (economics) and Moscow (history). NCU has state-of-the-art research infrastructure including the National Laboratory of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics (FAMO), the Center for Quantum Optics and the Interdisciplinary Center for Modern Technologies to name but a few, as well as modern teaching facilities comprising, among others, Collegium Humanisticum and the brand new University Sports Centre. The Centre for Astronomy in Piwnice near Toruń houses a unique 32-meter radio telescope. Spitsbergen (in the Arctic Sea) is home to NCU Polar Station. The university has also organized the Polish Historical Mission at the University of Würzburg. NCU researchers can boast a number of spectacular successes which include, among others, the design and construction of an Optical Coherence Tomography instrument, an ultra-modern device for medical eye examinations. The University Library holds an imposing collection of nearly 3 million printed volumes, periodicals and special collection items. NCU campus hosts the Academic Centre for Arts and Culture ‘Od Nowa’, one of the oldest students’ clubs in Poland. This has contributed to the Nicolaus Copernicus University’s position as one of the five best universities in Poland and it is also the reason why QS World University Ranking has placed NCU in the top 4% of universities in the world.

entityDescription:
Agrobit is an agtech startup that develops digital agriculture solutions and decision support systems (DSS) using crop images collected by optical instruments (smartphones, tractor-mounted cameras, drones). Agrobit's mission is to help farmers and technicians optimize/reduce the use of chemical inputs and water, reducing costs and the social and environmental impacts of agricultural activities, in line with the European Green Deal and the UN sustainability goals.
The flagship product is iAgro, an innovative DSS mobile app that transforms the smartphone into a 3D scanner and precision agriculture tool by exploiting artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), computer vision, 3D modeling (digital twin) and cloud computing technologies. The app allows you to obtain biometric and biophysical data of tree crops, export reports, maps and the history of the health status of the field. Using smartphones and AR algorithms, the user performs a 3D scan on the target plant which is then analyzed by computer vision and AI algorithms, creating its 3D model and automatically calculating biometric parameters (thickness, height, canopy volume), vigor parameters (LAI, LWA, TRV) and optimal doses of agrochemicals and water to be distributed in the field. By repeating the scans in multiple points of the field, the app allows you to generate vigor maps (useful for optimizing fertilization) and prescription maps for optimized phytosanitary treatments. The main competitive advantage lies in the quantification of the dose of agrochemical for each area of ​​the field (quantitative DSS) and in making the smartphone a simple, scalable, widespread, economic agronomic tool: crucial factors for the concrete diffusion of precision agriculture practices.
The iAgro app already use GNSS data but new developments are going on like integrating Sentinel-2 EO data to spatialize the app measurements at a higher scale. This approach will be used to calculate firstly crop yields and crop CO2 absorption, using data fusion techniques between iAgro in-field measurements and satellite vegetation indices.

Company description: Agrobit is an agtech startup that develops digital agriculture solutions and decision support systems (DSS) using crop images collected by optical instruments (smartphones, tractor-mounted cameras, drones). Agrobit's mission is to help farmers and technicians optimize/reduce the use of chemical inputs and water, reducing costs and the social and environmental impacts of agricultural activities, in line with the European Green Deal and the UN sustainability goals.
The flagship product is iAgro, an innovative DSS mobile app that transforms the smartphone into a 3D scanner and precision agriculture tool by exploiting artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), computer vision, 3D modeling (digital twin) and cloud computing technologies. The app allows you to obtain biometric and biophysical data of tree crops, export reports, maps and the history of the health status of the field. Using smartphones and AR algorithms, the user performs a 3D scan on the target plant which is then analyzed by computer vision and AI algorithms, creating its 3D model and automatically calculating biometric parameters (thickness, height, canopy volume), vigor parameters (LAI, LWA, TRV) and optimal doses of agrochemicals and water to be distributed in the field. By repeating the scans in multiple points of the field, the app allows you to generate vigor maps (useful for optimizing fertilization) and prescription maps for optimized phytosanitary treatments. The main competitive advantage lies in the quantification of the dose of agrochemical for each area of ​​the field (quantitative DSS) and in making the smartphone a simple, scalable, widespread, economic agronomic tool: crucial factors for the concrete diffusion of precision agriculture practices.
The iAgro app already use GNSS data but new developments are going on like integrating Sentinel-2 EO data to spatialize the app measurements at a higher scale. This approach will be used to calculate firstly crop yields and crop CO2 absorption, using data fusion techniques between iAgro in-field measurements and satellite vegetation indices.

TÜV SÜD Energietechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg (TÜV SÜD ET) was founded on 1 April 1997 under the name of “TÜV Energie- und Systemtechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg”. It was a spinoff from the former “Nuclear Technology and Radiation Protection” Division of TÜV Bayern Hessen Sachsen Südwest e.V. The company changed its name to “TÜV SÜD Energietechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg” with effect from 1 April 2006. It is a legal entity (LE) of the TÜV SÜD Group. The company provides
- advisory, inspection and certification services in the fields of energy technology, systems engineering and nuclear technology as well as
- radiation-protection services.
It does so primarily within its activities as an independent and impartial company of experts, not subject to professional instructions from third parties, which is consulted by the supervisory authorities of the German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg pursuant to Section 20 of the German Atomic Energy Act.
TÜV SÜD AG undertakes to exercise its shareholder rights in TÜV SÜD Energietechnik GmbH Baden-Wuerttemberg only to the effect that the impartiality, independence and technical authority of TÜV SÜD ET to provide its services without being subject to professional instructions by third parties will be guaranteed at all times and that TÜV SÜD ET will be able to fully meet all its responsibilities.
The main field of activity of TÜV SÜD ET lies in the testing and inspection of nuclear facilities within the context of nuclear licensing and/or supervisory procedures. The experts of the company and/or its predecessor organisation have operated in this area from the earliest times of peaceful use of nuclear energy. They can thus draw on over 50 years of experience, in particular with nuclear power stations in Baden-Wuerttemberg.
Since the German government’s 2011 decision to phase out nuclear energy by 2022, TÜV SÜD ET has stepped up its efforts to use its know-how in contracts located abroad or placed by international companies, e.g. manufacturers of nuclear components. This business line, while still under development at present, is to be expanded further by the development of new products and the establishment of a sales structure.
